name: Plaža Velika Duba (Živogošće Blato)
description: Hidden turquoise pebble cove under Biokovo between Živogošće and Blato, with a sea cave you can swim into. Narrow makadam road then a 5-10 min pine-forest walk from paid Blato parking; no cafes, loungers or souvenirs — carry water and shade. (fits D2)

name: Plaža Jezero (Duba Pelješka)
description: Shingle cove ~1km from the hamlet Duba Pelješka with no road access — reached by boat/kayak or a foot scramble. Named for a small lake behind it whose water spills across the beach into the sea; faces straight across to Biokovo. A genuine secret cove on north Pelješac. (fits D3)

name: Uvala Mokalo (Orebić)
description: Quiet pebble-and-rock 'skrivena uvala' just east of Orebić, the local alternative to busy Trstenica — clear water, calm hamlet feel, on the Korčula-ferry side of Pelješac. Low-effort swim/snorkel near the Orebić ferry. (fits D3)

name: Plaža i uvala Sutmiholjska (Mljet, Babino Polje)
description: Pebble/sand cove on Mljet's south coast near Babino Polje, OUTSIDE the national park (no ticket), far less hyped than Saplunara or Blace/Limuni. Open-sea facing with wild Mediterranean scrub — 'just pebbles underfoot and a view to the open sea'. Good late-afternoon swim away from NP crowds. (fits D4)

name: Rijeka Ljuta — izvor i kanjon (Konavle)
description: Croatia's southernmost river: a powerful ice-cold karst spring erupting under a 100m cliff and roaring through a short laurel-shaded canyon past centuries-old stone mills. Glacial even in June — a refreshing cold-plunge + scenic walk; distinct from the Konavoski Dvori restaurant at the same mills. (fits D12)

name: Plaža Danče (Dubrovnik)
description: The locals' city swim: a rocky platform with ladders into the sea just west of the old town below the Danče monastery, 5 min from Pile. Authentic 'pravi Dubrovnik' feel, great for sunset — a final-day swim without the Banje tourist scene. (fits D13)

name: Konoba Škojera (Trpanj, Pelješac)
description: Family konoba on the Trpanj waterfront known among Croatians for lamb and bread ispod peke (under the bell) and traditional Dalmatian dishes — a local peka stop near the Trpanj ferry. Reserve ahead; peka needs advance notice. (fits D3)

name: Vodopad Pjene (Bregava, Stolac)
description: The Bregava's prettiest waterfall just NE of Stolac (above the Begovina villas, by the Poplašić mill): a cave behind it, a small stone beach, swimming and water-jumping. Locals rent kayaks ~10 KM/hr at the bathing spot a few hundred metres downstream. Free, cool, self-rent — beats the Kravica crowds. Refine the exact platform on-site. (fits D4)

name: Avanturistički park Peć Mlini (Grude)
description: Adrenaline park at the karst spring of the Tihaljina, around old mills and the Ravlića cave (one of Europe's oldest inhabited caves, 5 KM). Headline: the longest zipline in BiH — 1km+, up to 62 km/h, 50 KM/person — plus sport climbing and a swimmable emerald spring. Daily 09:00-19:00 Apr-Oct, parking included. The optional via ferrata is separate/skippable. (fits D4)

name: Plaža Čivelj + Ostrožac iron bridge (Jablaničko jezero)
description: Lake beach in Gornje Paprasko ~8km from Jablanica on the M17, fitted with a diving/jump platform (skakaonica), gravel shore and concrete water access; pair it with the big tin reservoir bridge at Ostrožac (~43.6851,17.8305) that locals call 'bosanski Golden Gate'. Self-organised swim+jump stop; busy on weekends. (fits D5)

name: Ćevabdžinica Rota (Mostar)
description: Locals' repeat pick for the best ćevapi in Mostar since 1996 (Onešćukova 7, 2 min from Stari Most), with a fan-cooled garden for the June heat — the genuine local alternative to tourist-famous Tima Irma. Cheap quick-grab. (fits D5)

name: Stabanska jezera (Volujak)
description: Twin glacial lakes on Volujak's south flank almost no foreigner reaches; Veliko (1325m) is emerald, 9m deep, 16-20°C and swimmable, mountaineers wild-camp on its shore. A wilder, emptier alternative to Black/Trnovačko. Drive to Stabna village, then ~4.5km hike up; last road km is macadam. (fits D7)

name: Vidikovac Babina Greda (Piva)
description: Repeatedly called Piva's most beautiful viewpoint — and you can DRIVE to it (village Donji Unač, ~2.5km off the P14, ~9km from Plužine, paved). Covered shelters with benches/tables for a shaded picnic over the turquoise Piva reservoir, the canyon, and the Bioč-Maglić-Volujak + Durmitor wall. (fits D7)

name: Crvena greda (2164m), Durmitor
description: A local hiking blogger's 'most beautiful Durmitor viewpoint' — only ~4km / ~424m gain, walking-only (no scrambling or via ferrata), a relaxed half-day looking down on Jablan/Crno/Zminje lakes and across to Bobotov Kuk and the Tara canyon. Bigger view-per-effort than the crowded Bobotov Kuk slog. Trailhead at Bosača near Žabljak. (fits D8)

name: Dobri Do plateau wild-camp (Kamp Šarban)
description: Rolling pasture on Durmitor's south side ~3km from Sedlo pass toward Trsa (~15km from Žabljak, mostly macadam) — just OUTSIDE the NP boundary, so tent camping is free and tolerated, with a water source and open views under Prutaš/Bobotov Kuk. A basic marked pitch (Kamp Šarban) exists too; classic dawn launch for Prutaš/Škrčka/Bobotov Kuk. (fits D8)

name: Modro–Srablje–Valovito jezera (Sedlo ring)
description: Three small, quiet Durmitor lakes under Sedlena greda off the busy Black Lake circuit, on the scenic Žabljak→Sedlo→Trsa ring road. Modro (1609m, trout & wild ducks) sits with tiny Srablje and Valovito just over a moraine ridge — a short walk linking 'mountain eyes' with almost nobody around. (This is the Durmitor Modro jezero, not the Imotski one in data.) (fits D8)

name: Sinjajevina — Ckara vidikovac & paragliding plateau
description: Montenegro's vast (120,000ha) high pasture-plateau dotted with working katuns, almost untouched by tourism. The Ckara lodge area (1624m, ~12km / ~1h40 jeep-track from Mojkovac via Gacka) has the region's signature viewpoint and an official paragliding launch over the Tara valley — and a prime dark-sky / Milky-Way spot. Off-corridor; honest cost is the rough access track. (fits D8)

name: Eko Katun Goleš (Bjelasica, above Biogradska)
description: Working summer katun at ~1596m near Trabaljevo/Kolašin (jeep access, ~12km from Trebaljevo), 5 min from a viewpoint over Biogradska Lake. The draw is the real mountain table — own cheese, ham, handmade lemonade from the shepherds — plus simple eco-cabins to sleep up high; on the marked Bjelasica trails. Best as a D8→D9 transition; coord is the OSM Katun Goleš node (confirm exact pitch with host). (fits D9)

name: Uvala / Rt Veslo (Luštica)
description: Free wild cove on outer Luštica with cascading limestone steps, turquoise water, cliffs ideal for jumping and warm natural rock-pools. No infrastructure (small kiosk at Kamp Begović above); reach via the village track or by SUP/kayak. Distinct from the existing Žanjic/Dobreč coves. Bring water shoes (sharp rock, sea urchins); dangerous in wind. (fits D11)

name: Plaža Crvena stijena (Red Rock, Bar)
description: A ~50m red-cliff cove hidden behind Volujica hill near Bar, walled off so it stayed 'saved from mass tourism' — turquoise and crystal clear. Best by small boat/SUP from Bar; the only land route is an unlit tunnel (Rikavac) + a short swim (lantern needed), or a steep risky scramble locals advise against. A real secret-swim payoff if you go deep south. (fits D9)

name: Drobni Pijesak (Sveti Stefan ↔ Reževići)
description: A 240m ground-sand cove walled by green hills with blue-flag clear water, 3 min north of Rijeka Reževići yet minutes from the busiest resorts. Long boat-only so it stayed unspoiled; many still arrive by sea. Calm scenic alternative to crowded Sveti Stefan beaches — self-rent boat or a short trail in; only a small seasonal bar. (fits D11)

name: Zaboj viewpoint (Skadar, Komarno trail)
description: An abandoned stone hamlet on a rocky perch over Skadar's central meanders — the quiet alternative to the mobbed Pavlova strana, with views from Lovćen to Rumija. A marked circular trail leaves the road near Komarno village and follows old moss-grown paths (no thorn-bushwhacking). Same infinity-meander view, basically alone. Coord = Komarno trailhead. (fits D9)

name: Kafe Letrika (Kotor old town)
description: Small characterful cocktail/DJ bar by the Sea Gate in Kotor's old town (Stari grad 427) where locals and travellers mix for music and live DJs — the genuine-vibe spot over the generic tourist terraces (often paired with nearby Nitrox Pub for craft beer). A real night-out anchor inside the walls; confirm the exact door on arrival. (fits D11)
